sections.h2: Where is Pelham, Alabama, and what is it known for?
sections.html:
Pelham is a city in Shelby County and a suburb in the Birmingham metropolitan area, about 20 miles south of downtown Birmingham and 72 miles north of Montgomery. It incorporated on July 10, 1964, and takes its name from Confederate officer John Pelham.

The city covers about 39 square miles at roughly 830 feet of elevation and uses ZIP code 35124. Oak Mountain State Park, the largest state park in Alabama, lies within Pelham, so a lot of buyers who tour the city come for trails and lakes as much as for the housing.

The land has deeper roots than the city's age suggests. Shelbyville, the first Shelby County seat, stood within what are now Pelham's limits beginning in 1820, before the seat moved to Columbiana in 1826.

Pelham grew from 931 people in 1970 to 24,318 in 2020. Most of that jump came within two decades of incorporation.

The 2020 census counted 9,777 housing units in Pelham, with only 2.9 percent vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.7 percent and the rental vacancy rate was 5.1 percent. Both rates are low, so little housing sat empty when the census was taken.

sections.h2: Who lives in Pelham and what do homes look like?
sections.html:
The median age in Pelham was 39.4 in 2020, and 33.1 percent of households had children under 18. Married couple households made up 54.9 percent of the total, and about a quarter of households were one person living alone.

Most of Pelham's growth came after 1980, so much of the housing is a few decades old. Items that commonly come up on houses of that age include:

  • Roof coverings and flashing.
  • Heating and air systems.
  • Water heaters and original windows.

The county overall is 78.1 percent owner-occupied, so owner-occupants make up most of the housing.

sections.h2: How do I get to Pelham and around it?
sections.html:
US Route 31 runs directly through Pelham, and Interstate 65 serves the city with access from exits 242 and 246. ClasTran provides weekday dial-a-ride transit, and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport sits in the adjacent county.

Shelby County is also crossed by US 231 and US 280, and the Shelby County Airport handles general aviation. Because the interstate and US 31 have tied Shelby County to Jefferson County for decades, many Pelham residents commute north into Birmingham, while others work locally.

When you list a house, give buyers the real distance to the interstate and to Birmingham. In a suburb of this shape, commute length drives a lot of the conversation.

Pelham City Schools has run the city's public schools since July 1, 2014, when it split from the Shelby County school system. The district operates two elementary schools, one middle school and Pelham High School.

Before 2014, some parts of Pelham next to Chelsea attended Chelsea schools, and residents in those areas worried about the split because of distance. Houses in that part of town can still raise school boundary questions, so check assignments by address before you quote them.

The wider county has several private schools, including Briarwood Christian School and Westminster School at Oak Mountain, plus higher education choices such as Jefferson State's Shelby-Hoover campus and the University of Montevallo.

sections.h2: What does Shelby County add to the picture?
sections.html:
Shelby County has about 223,000 residents and ranks sixth in Alabama by population, with a seat in Columbiana. Growth in the county, including Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea, has been driven by access to the interstate and US 31.

The county also holds Oak Mountain Amphitheatre, the Aldrich Coal Mine Museum and the Heart of Dixie Railroad Museum, which round out the local lifestyle for buyers.

sections.h2: What does the geography of Pelham mean for a house?
sections.html:
Parts of Shelby County are crossed by the southern end of the Appalachians, including Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain, while other parts are flat farmland. The county drains mainly to the Cahaba River and the Coosa River.

A house on a slope can have drainage, retaining wall and foundation shifts to consider, while a house near a creek bed may deserve a closer look at the flood zone. We could not confirm Pelham-specific flood or hail statistics from an official source, so check the flood map for your parcel and ask your insurer about local claims history.

sections.h2: How is the City of Pelham run, and who handles permits?
sections.html:
Pelham operates under the Mayor and Council Act, with the mayor as chief executive and the council acting somewhat like a board of directors. The city lists its own police chief, fire chief, finance director and city clerk, building inspector, permits clerk, revenue director, parks manager, waterworks superintendent and librarian, along with a golf director.

That matters when you sell because several of those offices touch a house: the building inspector and permits clerk for work done without paperwork, the waterworks department for utility accounts, and the revenue department for business and other local licenses. If an owner finished a basement or added a room, ask the city whether a permit was pulled before you list.

sections.h2: Why did Shelby County grow so quickly around Pelham?
sections.html:
Shelby County's history explains the pattern. The county was founded on February 7, 1818, grew through farming, with soybeans now ahead of cotton, and was crossed early by the Louisville and Nashville Railroad and later by US 31. Interstate 65 then tied it more tightly to Jefferson County to the north.

The county grew from 38,037 people in 1970 to 66,298 in 1980 and 223,024 in 2020. Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea all absorbed that suburban development, which is why a Pelham seller competes with houses in several nearby cities, each with its own school district.

sections.h2: What do Pelham sellers pay when the deed is recorded, and when are taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama Code section 40-22-1 sets a recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value on a deed, paid before the probate judge records it. A $200,000 sale produces $200 under that formula, and the recording fee is separate.

The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. The Shelby County offices in Columbiana hold the parcel records and can supply a payoff figure.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a good fit for a Pelham owner?
sections.html:
A cash sale is worth considering when you want a firm date and no repairs. Pelham examples include:

  • A house from the decades of fast growth that needs a roof and air system before it would pass a buyer's inspection.
  • An estate property the heirs do not want to maintain.
  • An owner moving for work who cannot wait through a long listing period.

Compare any offer to the likely net from a listing after repairs, fees and the carrying cost of the months a house may sit. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays the closing costs, and take time to read the contract before you sign. We buy Pelham houses as they are and you are free to decline.

faqs.q: What county is Pelham, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Pelham is in Shelby County, in the Birmingham metropolitan area.

faqs.q: How far is Pelham from Birmingham?
faqs.a: Downtown Birmingham is about 20 miles north of Pelham, reachable by US 31 or Interstate 65.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Pelham?
faqs.a: The Alabama Department of Revenue says property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Does Pelham have its own school system?
faqs.a: Yes. Pelham City Schools was established on July 1, 2014 and runs two elementary schools, a middle school and Pelham High School.
